canonical_statement: For every finite family of independent measurable real random variables X_i on a probability space, almost surely bounded by a_i and b_i, and every epsilon >= 0, the probability that the centered sum is at least epsilon is at most exp((-2*epsilon^2)/(sum_i (b_i-a_i)^2)).
domain_and_universes: universes u v; I : Type v with Fintype I; Omega : Type u with MeasurableSpace Omega; mu : Measure Omega with IsProbabilityMeasure mu; X : I -> Omega -> Real; a b : I -> Real; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: forall i, almost everywhere omega with respect to mu, X i omega is in Set.Icc (a i) (b i)
conclusion: mu.real {omega | epsilon <= sum_i (X_i(omega) - integral X_i dmu)} <= Real.exp ((-2 * epsilon^2) / sum_i (b_i-a_i)^2)
foundation_profile: Lean 4 dependent type theory; classical/noncomputable Bochner integration is permitted; no proof is supplied by this phase.
tcb_profile: Lean kernel, repository-pinned Lean toolchain, and repository-pinned mathlib dependency closure.
computation_profile: Noncomputable measure and Bochner-integral expressions; no oracle or experimental result.

degenerate_cases: The target includes the empty family, epsilon = 0, and zero total squared width. Lean real division fixes the denominator-zero syntax: x / 0 = 0, so the displayed right side is exp 0 = 1 in that case. No positivity premise on the denominator is silently added.
